title: Reduce 66-grade extraction from 128 to optimal 68 runs (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the exact minimum of **68 complete executions** for extracting arbitrary diagonal blocks on 66 nonzero grades by equally weighted sign conjugations. Yiyang's merged #5037 uses 128 complete root executions at this grade count.

```text
128-run Walsh extraction
  -> 68-run Paley sign extraction
  -> exact accumulator division by 4 and 17
  -> the same dyadic block-diagonal output
```

Claim type: scoped algebraic proof with an exact finite sign certificate. Rank and three-column divisibility give the lower bound; the classical Paley order-68 Hadamard matrix attains it. The application and exact-grid wrapper are the new step. Paley's construction and character averaging are credited methods, not claimed inventions. The reduction saves 60 complete executions; copying, signs, accumulation and exact division are additional work. No wall-clock gain, native invoice change or new κ is claimed.

Only six files under `research/grade-sign-extraction/` are added. The proof applies at arbitrary nonzero grade dimensions, with arbitrary off-diagonal blocks, and includes exact integer divisibility by 17. The wrapper is applied once at the root; repeated input copies earn no productive credit.

## Evidence

- **Before:** #5037's source-bound extraction note specifies `K=2^ceil(log2(H+1))`, hence 128 at 66 grades. **After:** the exact sign design uses 68 rows, and the matching scoped lower bound rules out 66 and 67.
- At head `eb0c12811253174a6a7834c118e2cf827cc9b706`, normal and optimized warning-strict CPython 3.12.15 replay pass. The final Git-free invocations took about 0.35 seconds each, well below the 120-second registered limits. These are check durations, not physical performance measurements.
- Exact evidence includes 2,346 full Gram entries, 28 dense/triangular unequal-grade fixtures with 1,712 output components, a six-coordinate variable-denominator fixture recovered through the integer divider, 8,201 signed exact divisions and 11 rejection controls. Three disposable semantic corruptions reject. Removing a redundant remainder guard preserves behavior because the quotient postcondition still enforces exactness; it is not counted as a rejected semantic corruption.
- Registered replay, AST/function-bound checks, six-file committed-byte/full-source-history preflight and official export integrity pass. Both normal and optimized standalone checks also pass in a read-only Git-free export with `PATH=/nonexistent`; all seven exported files remain byte-identical. The verifier writes no files and imports no predecessor executable.

From the worktree root, reproduce with the actual local interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/grade-sign-extraction
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/grade-sign-extraction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/grade-sign-extraction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/grade-sign-extraction --check-source-history
```

Expected direct output includes `PASS_GRADE_SIGN_EXTRACTION`, `runs: 68`, `literal_cases: 28` and `signed_exact_divisions: 8201`. On another host substitute its CPython 3.12 path. The dimension-uniform claim rests on the written proof, not extrapolation from fixtures. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Limitations

The optimality contract requires equal positive weights and grade-constant ±1 conjugations that work for every permitted off-diagonal block. Unequal weights, complex phases, independent input/output maps and additional sparsity are outside it. The exact divider needs the proved output-grid/divisibility premise; arbitrary division by 68 is not a free dyadic operation.

Actual native shears, recursive source/exit matching, rounded arithmetic, physical ownership/movement/restoration, stock, BIT transfer and outer admission remain open. No full physical tariff, selected cold replay, native/Lean/Docker suite or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. The selected frontier is unchanged. Python's bounded managed-runtime allocation and diagnostic limitations are documented in README.

## Related open work

- #5106 studies the actual two-full fresh-D endpoint and gives a coherent-gauge obstruction. This wrapper assumes a completed same-grade program and does not discharge that endpoint or re-check its counts.
- No other open PR on the 66-grade equal-weight sign-extraction minimum was found in the inspected coverage. The refreshed snapshot covers 333 open PRs and 4,251 Discussion records with complete reported pagination; sparse local notes, arbitrary unseen diffs and unpublished work remain outside complete coverage.

## Open next questions

- Bind one literal native caller from #5037 to the completed graded extraction contract, preserving every source, exit and complement. Coherent shears and whole-job recursive matching remain blockers.
- Compare the complete physical tariff of the 68-run and 128-run wrappers, including signed copies, workspace reuse, accumulation and exact division by 17, once such a caller exists.

## CI notes

**CI blocked upstream.** [Run 39933925464](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39933925464), for contribution head `eb0c12811253174a6a7834c118e2cf827cc9b706`, failed in `plan` / `Onboarding helper tests`; `replay` was skipped. The log reports 408 tests, eight failures and 17 skips. No hosted package replay or mathematical acceptance is claimed.

The checkout log identifies tested merge `5b6a029383b29e00c5684eeba983eba23b896f0c`, combining this contribution with main `20a1e31bc6009b9b3f4d084bbaadc6350e34fcba`. This PR changes only the six files under `research/grade-sign-extraction/`; it changes no shared scripts, tests, workflow or historical fixture.

Two upstream fixture problems account for the eight failures:

- Seven failing subcases in `tests/test_research_descendant_source_roles.py` stop at `working source drift: scripts/check_research_commit.py`, before their expected helper/history-test diagnostic or acceptance. The historical `research/isolated-descendant-bytecode/SOURCES.json` still declares that script as an input with SHA256 `ecf206a82bf1f4e748efb6cc639919582050d173b3537ec12f7265a4f7b55ead`, while the tested main version hashes to `28fed1e156fe8601633ed453f682a158cb15e94981e6c89ed96ae72ffc9d0c6f`. The expected diagnostics include `source blob provenance mismatch: scripts/research_package.py`, `source SHA256 provenance mismatch: scripts/research_package.py` and the corresponding `tests/test_research_source_history.py` messages. The unchanged fixture copies the current shared script before authenticating it against the historical live-input pin.
- `tests/test_research_onboarding.py::OverlapTests::test_report_survives_a_cp1252_stdout` copies only `scripts/find_overlap.py` into its temporary repository. The current helper imports `git_source_env` from `research_package`, but that module is absent in the fixture, giving `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'research_package'`.

[Upstream commit 862ac2a0f](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/862ac2a0fecbf1c613f7f07957f8c17b4b319bf3) changes both shared scripts and is an ancestor of the tested main base. Its diff and the base's actual bytes confirm the new import and historical-pin mismatch. No shared-code fix is included here.

The same eight failures, with the same diagnostics, are independently visible in [PR #5116](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5116), “Implement complete owned query streams on selected signed records”, head `ee4bebf4bb1d441bbbcd43ff4bc2bcb2734a679e`, [run 39933826517](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39933826517). This comparison is limited to the failed onboarding-job logs; that contribution's mathematics was not reviewed or replayed.

Both registered package commands and the committed/source-history/export checks passed locally at the unchanged contribution head, as recorded above. Upstream onboarding repair and a successful hosted replay remain outstanding. No DONE has been posted.
